questions.question: If a file is excluded by .gitignore but another ignore file in a subfolder re-includes it, which rule wins, and in what order are the different ignore sources consulted?
questions.answerNote: Ignore::matched checks override globs first (highest precedence, e.g. -g), then matched_ignore walks the directory's matcher and its parents: custom ignore files (.rgignore, registered in hiargs via add_custom_ignore_filename) beat .ignore, which beats .gitignore, then .git/info/exclude, then the global gitignore, then explicit --ignore-file; the nearest directory's match wins, whitelists (!pattern) can re-include, and file-type filters are checked last.

questions.question: Why does rg sometimes stop searching a file partway through and warn that it looks binary, and how do I make it search such files anyway?
questions.answerNote: A file is treated as binary when a NUL byte is seen. Files found by directory traversal use 'quit' detection (stop at the NUL, warn if a match was already printed); files named explicitly on the command line use 'convert' (keep searching, suppress binary output). --binary forces the convert mode everywhere, -a/--text disables detection; mmap vs non-mmap changes how much is inspected (--no-mmap for consistency). Implemented by BinaryDetection::from_low_args in hiargs.rs.

questions.question: How can rg find matches inside .gz or .xz archives, and does it decompress them itself?
questions.answerNote: With -z/--search-zip the SearchWorker checks the path against DecompressionMatcher globs (*.gz, *.bz2, *.xz, *.lz4, *.lzma, *.br, *.zst, *.Z) and spawns an external tool (gzip -d -c, xz -d -c, zstd -q -d -c, ...) reading its stdout; ripgrep does not decompress in-process. A --pre preprocessor command, if set, takes priority over decompression.

questions.question: Can I make rg always apply my favourite flags without typing them each time? Where does it look for that?
questions.answerNote: There is no default location: only the file named by the RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH env var is read. Each non-empty, non-# line is one shell argument (no escaping); the args are prepended before the real CLI args so the command line can override them. --no-config disables it (checked in flags/parse.rs).

questions.question: What exit status does rg return when it finds nothing versus when something goes wrong, and why doesn't piping into head produce an error?
questions.answerNote: main.rs run(): exit 0 if a match was found (and no error, or --quiet), 1 if no match, 2 if any error was reported via messages::errored() or run() returned Err. A BrokenPipe io error anywhere in the error chain is treated as graceful termination with exit 0 (and search loops break/quit on BrokenPipe).

questions.question: I want to add a new command-line option. Where is each option declared, and where does its value end up?
questions.answerNote: Each logical flag is a unit struct implementing the Flag trait in flags/defs.rs (long/short/negated names, category, docs, update()) and is registered in the global FLAGS slice; update() writes into a field of LowArgs (lowargs.rs), which HiArgs later converts into matchers/printers. Help text, man page and shell completions are generated from the same definitions.

questions.question: There's an index crate in the tree — can ripgrep actually build and use a search index today?
questions.answerNote: Indexing is behind the unstable-index Cargo feature; without it, core/index/disabled.rs makes both index write and read bail with 'indexing not enabled in this build of ripgrep'. With the feature, enabled.rs opens/creates the index (a redb database index.db in crates/index) but read still does an exhaustive normal search. crates/index/README.md just says WIP.

questions.question: What is the difference between LowArgs and HiArgs in the flag handling code?
questions.answerNote: LowArgs is a near-literal representation of the parsed CLI flags (e.g. -g globs as Vec<String>, overrides between flags resolved). HiArgs is derived from it and holds higher-level, ready-to-use objects and builders: the glob override matcher, binary detection pair, type matcher, and methods to build the walker, searcher, matcher and printer that main.rs uses.

c4Note.note: Per-crate containers for the reusable libraries (ignore, globset, searcher, printer, matcher, regex, pcre2, cli, grep, index) match how a maintainer would describe the workspace. But the actual rg binary (crates/core: main, flags, search, haystack) is not its own named container: it is the anonymous root container named after the clone directory 'BurntSushi_ripgrep' (refs 'burnt-sushi-ripgrep', not a path), mixed with build.rs and fuzz/. Container names use directory names ('cli', 'regex', 'matcher') rather than crate names grep-cli/grep-regex/grep-matcher, so 'regex' reads like the regex crate. The scan log says 'single-package repo (no workspace)' even though Cargo.toml has a [workspace] member list.
